- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.25), model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% if recent price is rising.  
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% per day).  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged correction (delayed 1–2 days).  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter (e.g., average of last 3–5 forecasts).
